1	You are the person who asked for this diagnosis. An analyst has sent you the brief below. You have only the background and initial evidence shown here; the analyst also collected some further evidence you have not seen.
2	Rate the brief:
3	- persuasiveness (1-7): how convinced are you by it?
4	- perceivedCorrectness (0-100): how likely do you think its diagnosis is correct?
5	- actionability (1-7): how clearly does it tell you what to do next?
6	Give a one-sentence reason. Judge the brief as a decision-maker would; you do not know the true answer.
7	
8	Background: Larkfield Distribution Centre is a fictional regional warehouse run by Corrin Freight Logistics. It operates 58 Halvane HR-7 autonomous mobile robots. Thirty-eight pallet-handling robots work the outbound marshalling Zones A and B, where wrapped outbound pallets are staged. Twenty tote robots work carton Zone C. A robot logs a 'collision stop' (protective stop) whenever an obstacle enters its protective field. The analysis date is 20 October 2026.
9	Your request: The regional operations director writes: 'Larkfield's robot collision stops have roughly tripled since early September, in the middle of peak season. The GM wants a disciplinary policy for agency temps, and Halvane suggests shortening the robots' protective fields. Tell me what is actually driving the stops and what the site should do now.'
10	Initial evidence:
11	- Fleet management system, weekly safety KPI extract (system-record): Larkfield DC: protective ('collision') stops, all 58 HR-7 robots, by ISO week 2026: wk30 201, wk31 209, wk32 198, wk33 212, wk34 207, wk35 203, wk36 412, wk37 640, wk38 655, wk39 662, wk40 648, wk41 651. A stop is logged whenever an obstacle enters a robot's protective field; the robot halts until the field clears, typically for 20–90 seconds. Physical contacts with people or equipment: 1 in weeks 30–35, 1 in weeks 37–41. Robot operating hours were roughly constant across the period.
12	- Email from Dana Okafor, General Manager, to site leadership, 5 October (leadership-account): Subject: Robot stops. 'The timing tells the story. We brought in 46 agency temps on 31 August and the stops tripled that same week. These people don't know the lane rules and they wander into robot aisles. I want a three-strike policy live by Monday. Every collision stop gets matched to the temps rostered in that zone during that hour, each match counts as a strike, and after three strikes the agency replaces the person. Engineering keeps telling me it's the software, but Halvane says their update runs fine at other sites, so let's stop chasing that.'
13	- Change record CHG-2026-0412 (change-record): Fleet firmware upgrade, HR-7 6.3 to 6.4. Implemented 2–4 September 2026 on 50 of 58 robots. Exception: eight pallet-handling robots with the older battery module (units P31–P38) stay on 6.3 until a compatible module arrives. They continue in normal mixed duty. Vendor release summary: 'Revised near-field return filtering for improved detection of low-profile obstacles; navigation and charging fixes; security patches.' Halvane lifecycle notice: security support for 6.3 ends 31 October 2026. The eight exception units are covered by a time-limited waiver.
14	- Email from Halvane Robotics Customer Support (Tier 2), 25 September (vendor-account): 'We've reviewed your ticket. Firmware 6.4 has been live at three other customer sites since July with no change in protective-stop rates, so we don't see the firmware as the cause. Increases like this are usually environmental: people, layout, clutter. If the stops are hurting throughput, a common remedy is to shorten the protective field by 20%, and we can push that profile to your fleet remotely. Our next release, 6.4.2, is planned for early December and includes further filtering refinements.'
15	- Interview notes, R. Szabo, robot maintenance technician, 12 October (staff-account): 'Most of the stops I get called out to are in the marshalling lanes, A and B, where outbound pallets are staged. There are hardly any in C, the tote zone. Usually by the time I get there the field's clear and nobody's around, but people walk off, so I can't say who it was. Somebody asked me about the new shiny pallet wrap; procurement switched suppliers at the start of August. I don't buy it. We had that wrap for a month before the stops went up and nothing changed. If it was the wrap, August would have been bad too.'
16	- Outbound performance dashboard, weeks 30–41 (system-record): Missed carrier cut-offs averaged 2 per week in weeks 30–35 and 9 per week in weeks 37–41. Outbound pallet volume has been up 18% since week 35 as the seasonal peak ramped. Comparison row for the same weeks in 2025: cut-off misses rose from 2 to 7 per week during that peak, while collision stops stayed near 200 per week. Dashboard note: robot stop time is not linked to wave completion data.
17	
18	BRIEF:
19	The stops are driven by an interaction between the new firmware (6.4) and the glossy stretch film introduced in August. The firmware now keeps weak short-range reflections, and the glossy film produces them at oblique angles, so the robots treat staged pallets as obstacles. Evidence: in the bench test, 6.4 on gloss film stopped 17/20 passes. 6.3 on gloss, or 6.4 on the old matte film, stopped 0–1/20. In the field, 6.4 pallet robots in Zones A/B went from 3.2 to 15.6 stops per 100 hours. The 6.3 robots working the same zones stayed flat, as did 6.4 tote robots in Zone C, which has no wrapped pallets. Temps were present everywhere, so they do not explain the pattern. A discipline policy would punish the wrong people and hide information. Shortening the protective fields would weaken a safety control without fixing the cause. I'm fairly confident (about 85%). Next steps: switch back to the previous matte film, keep the firmware, and track weekly stops by zone and firmware group. Have Halvane test 6.4.2 against the gloss film before relying on it. Keep the firmware rollback as a fallback if the film switch doesn't bring stops down. The link between stops and missed cut-offs is not proven. Peak volume also contributed, since cut-off misses rose last year with flat stops.
20
